articles.title: Diana’s brother says Harry and Meghan face 'cancerous' press
articles.summary: Earl Spencer says that he can see echoes of Princess Diana's treatment from the press in the way Harry and Meghan are scrutinised.
articles.body:
Earl Spencer has told the BBC that there are similarities between the way his sister Diana, Princess of Wales and the Duke and Duchess of Sussex have been treated by the press.

He said Princess Diana was "brought low" by press criticism of her and that it is a "pity" to see echoes of that in Harry and Meghan's lives now.

He added that people should learn from Princess Diana's example, and that for anyone being "destroyed daily" by the tabloid press, it must be a "cancerous influence" on their lives.

The full interview with Laura Kuenssberg, Princess Diana: My Sister's Story, will be available on iPlayer from 16:00 and broadcast on BBC One at 18:30 BST on Sunday.

articles.title: What's the future look like for the PGA Tour's new event in North Carolina?
articles.summary: The Biltmore Championship is Asheville's first PGA Tour event in 84 years, aiding recovery after Hurricane Helene.
articles.body:
ASHEVILLE, N.C. - With the Blue Ridge Mountains framing the PGA Tour's Biltmore Championship Asheville , an event now in full swing at The Cliffs at Walnut Cove in Arden, many spectators were seeing a PGA Tour event live for the first time.

Off the green, the audience politely applauded the players in the tournament that began with nearly 130 competitors.

Griffin Collins, an Atlanta resident, said he had attended PGA Tour events before that and said the Biltmore Championship Asheville stands up to the best of them.

"It's super cool. The course is beautiful," he said.

Collins attended the Biltmore Championship Asheville with friends the day before his wedding in the city. It was a bonus for the golf fan, as the wedding was planned before the PGA Tour was announced.

It's the first PGA Tour event in Asheville in 84 years, hosted on the Jack Nicklaus-designed course at a venue more than 23,000 square feet, which opened in 2005.

"It is a beautiful day to showcase Asheville and Western North Carolina to the entire golfing world," Governor Josh Stein said on the second morning of the tournament. "It's going to show these gorgeous mountains to viewers all over the world, and people are going to say to themselves, 'I want to go there,' and that's what we want to do ― let the world know Western North Carolina is open for business."

Western North Carolina shines for Biltmore Championship Asheville

Without a fog delay, as on the first day of the prestigious tournament, the professional men's golfers began the second day of the inaugural tournament under clear skies and sunshine, playing their way around the course and moving closer to claiming the victory, the custom-made gold-and-silver trophy and a cut of the $5 million purse.

The Biltmore Championship Asheville is the first of eight in the FedEx Fall Series, played after the Tour Championship, which finalizes eligibility for the 2027 PGA Tour Season.

Collins was rooting for the Vanderbilt University alum Gordon Sargent.

"Hopefully he can get back in the league and get back up there," he said.

Before Stein made his rounds of the holes, he paused to comment on the players with local ties.

"It's great that some of the most talented golfers in the world are North Carolinians. We have J.T. Polston and Webb Simpson competing here, and we're cheering hard for them," he said.

Post-Helene economy, recovery boost in WNC

The Biltmore Championship Asheville was secured through a $2.4 million four-year agreement between the PGA Tour and co-sponsors Biltmore, of the famed Biltmore Estate and Biltmore House, and Explore Asheville.

More than 10,000 guests were expected to attend the sold-out four-day event, with more than 2,000 out-of-state visitors, according to Explore Asheville. More than 1,100 volunteers registered to help before and during the tournament.

Anna Catherine, a Hickory resident and staff member at the University of North Carolina Asheville, signed up to volunteer three days over the weekend.

"It's a great way to get out and meet people and give back, which is one of the core pillars of what we do for the community, and I wanted to do my part," she said. "I wanted to be part of what makes it special and bringing people back to Asheville."

The future of Biltmore Championship Asheville, WNC

Stein said the PGA Tour is expected to significantly boost the region's economy, generating millions of dollars over the four-day weekend, accelerating WNC's recovery progress since Hurricane Helene, which arrived as a tropical storm in the fall of 2024.

Collins said he and his fiancée had visited Asheville many times before and after Helene, ultimately choosing an undisclosed venue in the city to exchange vows and celebrate.

"Our venue was under five feet of water but they rebuilt everything, so we felt good with going there since they were back up and running," he said.

During the four-day visit, he, his wedding party, and guests planned to venture outside The Cliffs at Walnut Cove to local businesses, including a welcome party at Hi-Wire Brewing, with food catered by Bear's Smokehouse BBQ , also a PGA Tour food vendor.

Collins said he planned to return for the next years of the Biltmore Championship Asheville.

Stein said the Biltmore Championship Asheville aims to accelerate the region's recovery, adding that there have been "encouraging indicators" of taxable sales in 2026, compared to before the historic storm.

"We see progress being made, but we know there's a lot more work to do," Stein said.

He said employment in Buncombe County hadn't fully rebounded , but that the way to boost employment is to increase local money circulation.

Asheville's unemployment rate was 3.3% in July 2026, according to the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics.

"We want the world to know what we know about Western North Carolina. It's so beautiful; the people are nice, they're friendly, they're kind. The food is great, the beer is good, the crafts are beautiful. There's just so much to enjoy in Western North Carolina; we want more people to come here and spend their money."

Tiana Kennell is the food and dining reporter for the Asheville Citizen Times, part of USA TODAY Co., covering the food and beverage industry and PGA Tour's Biltmore Championship Asheville. articles.title: Manuel Elvira colidera el BMW PGA Championship con Alejandro del Rey a un golpe
articles.standfirst: Los españoles, de lleno en la pelea por ganar en Wentworth frente a los Spaun, Niemann, McIlroy, Aberg...
articles.summary: Los españoles, de lleno en la pelea por ganar en Wentworth frente a los Spaun, Niemann, McIlroy, Aberg...
articles.body: La actuación de los jugadores españoles en la tercera ronda del BMW PGA Championship fue extraordinaria, hasta el punto de que dos miembros de la ‘Armada’ están de lleno en la pelea por el torneo más prestigioso de la temporada regular del DP World Tour. Manuel Elvira es colíder en Wentworth, la casa del Circuito Europeo, junto al italiano Filippo Celli, ambos muy consistentes esta semana. Este domingo volverán a compartir partido, pero esta vez será en el ‘estelar’. El cántabro, que buscará estrenar su palmarés profesional mañana, firmó unos segundos nueve hoyos muy buenos, logrando un birdie de mérito en el 12 y un par complicado en el 13. "Creo que estoy listo [para ganar], he estado jugando bien las últimas semanas. Obviamente, los resultados no me acompañaban, pero esta semana logré mantener la calma y simplemente disfrutar", apuntó Manuel tras finalizar la ronda. El día del movimiento en el mítico recorrido de Surrey fue precioso, con Alejandro del Rey (ocho birdies sin bogeys) y el estadounidense Johannes Veerman (204) firmando la mejor vuelta del día (64 golpes) para subir como la espuma en la clasificación y situarse a un golpe de la cabeza. El madrileño, un jugador que cuando está inspirado bate récords, vuela por debajo del radar esta semana entre tanto gallo, pero su candidatura para el triunfo es firme. Junto a ellos, con 204 golpes, JJ Spaun, todo un ganador del US Open (2025) que este año ya levantó el Texas Open. También hizo 64 el noruego Kristoffer Reitan, otro ganador este año en el PGA Tour y y entre los convocados por Luke Donald para acudir a la concentración de Adare Manor -sede de la Ryder Cup 2027- de hace unos días. Reitan está en el grupo de 205 golpes en el que también se encuentran Rory McIlroy, Joaquín Niemann, Adam Scott, Ryan Fox, Ludvig Aberg, Bob MacIntyre o Matt Wallace. Imposible pedir más nivel al torneo. La nómina de estrellas bien posicionadas no acaba ahí y tampoco hay que olvidar al español Nacho Elvira, uno de los jugadores más regulares del circuito este año, que con 208 en el acumulado mantiene posibilidades de victoria o, cuanto menos, de anotarse un ‘top 10’ que lo consolidaría en la pelea por las tarjetas del PGA Tour. Eugenio López-Chacarra, con 209, también aspira a un gran resultado, así como Ángel Ayora (210). La ‘Armada’ está que sale en uno de los torneos de más nivel del DPWT. David Puig y Rafa Cabrera (212) también están completando una semana muy positiva.

articles.title: BMW PGA Championship 2026: Rory McIlroy two off pace as Manuel Elvira and Filippo Celli share third-round lead at Wentworth
articles.summary: Rory McIlroy among group of 20 players who will go into final round of BMW PGA Championship within four shots of the lead; watch final round live on Sky Sports Golf on Sunday
articles.body:
Rather remarkably, 20 players will go into Sunday within four shots of the lead, including Rory McIlroy, who produced a box-office finish, sending the patrons into delirium on the 18th by making an eagle to move within two shots of the pace-setting duo at 11 under par.

McIlroy equalled four other players - Adam Scott, Joaquin Niemann, Davis Bryant and Kristoffer Reitan - to finish tied for sixth on the leaderboard through 54 holes.

In windy conditions, Spain's Alejandro Del Rey and American duo Johannes Veerman and JJ Spaun had all been tied with Celli and Elvira at 12 under par late in the third round.

Del Rey and Veerman had enjoyed epic days on the course, each shooting low scores of eight-under 64 to shoot up the leaderboard.

Celli, however, rose to make four birdies on his back nine, to jump above the chasing pack, alongside Elvira, and benefitted from an incredible bit of luck on his last hole.

His approach shot ricocheted off a wooden bulkhead lining the stream and somehow missed the water, instead skirting into the greenside bunker. From there he would make birdie to card a third-round 69.

"I'm very happy because today was very tough," the 26-year-old Italian said. "It was windy out there. So I'm happy with how I handled the situation. Sometimes the wind changed a bit, so it wasn't easy.

"I was very patient through the front nine because I knew that on the back nine, I could have like more chances to make some birdies."

Elvira also made a birdie on his last hole, to post a four-under 68, and said after his round he "feels ready" to claim his debut tournament on the DP World Tour.

Plenty of other high-profile players also remain firmly in contention at the top of a bunched leaderboard, with Robert MacIntyre impressing to go five under through what was a flawless, bogey-free back nine, as he rose to tied-11th at 10 under par, alongside Ludvig Åberg, Ryan Fox, Matt Wallace and Sam Bairstow.

"That was a grind out there," Scott, who had to battle to move to finish two shots off the lead, said. "I saw all these good scores up on the board, but it didn't feel like that was really doable.

"It was one step forward and a couple of steps back out there. Very hard to get in a rhythm. Hard to feel like you had a number where you could attack."

Elsewhere, first round co-leader Aaron Rai struggled to advance his score on Saturday, as he finished his day at nine under par. Matt Fitzpatrick, meanwhile, surged up the leaderboard to tie his compatriot, Rai, three back from the lead, alongside halfway leader Ryan Gerard, Alex Noren and Jordan Smith.

McIlroy: I will play aggressively if I need to

It felt like the Northern Irishman was looking for a spark throughout his third round, with McIlroy battling to go one over through his front nine.

The eighth hole has been his nemesis all week, with McIlroy cancelling out an early birdie on the fourth with a bogey on the eighth before adding another on the ninth.

It means McIlroy has gone three over on the eighth hole over his first three rounds.

The reigning Masters champion, who can usurp Patrick Reed at the top of the Race to Dubai Rankings with a second-place finish at the top of the leaderboard this week, found his groove, making birdie on the 12th, thanks to some excellent chipping.

He ended his third round with a flourish, striping a three-wood 375 yards down the fairway on the 17th hole on his way to make birdie, before stuffing an approach from 230 yards out to within a few feet of the hole.

McIlroy holed out for eagle to an enormous roar from the fans in the grandstand.

With so many players in contention, and crucial Race to Dubai rankings points in the balance for the world No 2, McIlroy insisted he would play aggressively on the back nine.

"Sunday is going to be interesting," McIlroy said.

"There are a lot of people around the leaders. I think the conditions over the last couple of days are the reason why no one has got away from the pack, just because it has played so tricky and difficult.

"I'll probably try not to look at the leaderboards on the front nine, and if I need to play a little bit more aggressively on the back, I'll do it."

articles.title: BMW PGA Championship: Eagle leaves Rory McIlroy two off the lead at Wentworth
articles.summary: Rory McIlroy stands two strokes behind the third-round leaders heading into the final day after a three-under 72 at the BMW PGA Championship at Wentworth.
articles.body:
13 M Elvira (Spa), F Celli (Ita); -12 J Veerman (US), A Del Rey (Spa) JJ Spaun (US)

Selected others: -11 R McIlroy (NI), A Scott (AUS); -10 S Bairstow (Eng), M Wallace (Eng), R MacIntyre (Sco); -9 J Smith (Eng), M Fitzpatrick (Eng), A Rai (Eng); -7 R Fisher (Eng), S Lowry (Ire); -6 A Fitzpatrick (Eng); -5 D Law (Sco), J Rose (Eng), E Ferguson (Sco), T Hatton (Eng)

Rory McIlroy finished with a superb eagle to move two shots off the lead heading into the final day of the BMW PGA Championship at Wentworth.

Northern Ireland's world number two made a three on the par-five 18th to stay in contention with a three-under 69 leaving him on 11 under.

Spain's Manuel Elvira and Italy's Filippo Celli share the lead after both made birdies on the final hole to leave them 13 under.

But there is a congested leaderboard with 20 players within four strokes of the lead.

Alejandro Del Rey, JJ Spaun and Johannes Veerman are one shot behind with an exciting finish in store on Sunday.

McIlroy is attempting to win a record-equalling eighth Race to Dubai title and can boost his hopes by securing the second Wentworth title of his career.

"There are a lot of people around the leaders," he said after another round in blustery conditions.

"I think the conditions over the last couple of days are the reason why no-one has got away from the pack, just because it has played so tricky and difficult.

"I'll probably try not to look at the leaderboards on the front nine, and if I need to play a little bit more aggressively on the back, I'll do it."

articles.title: ‘Cats go undefeated in non-con play with win over Tulane
articles.summary: MANHATTAN (KSNT) — K-State stays undefeated in non-conference play. The Wildcats defeated the Tulane Green Wave Saturday afternoon, 31-20. Tulane opened up t...
articles.body:
MANHATTAN ( KSNT ) — K-State stays undefeated in non-conference play.

The Wildcats defeated the Tulane Green Wave Saturday afternoon, 31-20.

Tulane opened up the scoring just under the eight-minute mark with a nine-yard quarterback run for a touchdown to lead 7-0.

K-State would not score in the first quarter.

In the second, Luis Rodriguez kicked in a 23-yard field goal to cut the deficit to 7-3.

A few minutes later, running back Jay Harris had a one-yard rush to give the 'Cats the 10-7 lead.

With a little over two minutes remaining, Avery Johnson would pick up a huge 66-yard gain to set up the first down. He'd rush again the following play, this time for seven yards, to grab the touchdown. K-State has the 17-7 lead.

A 58-yard field goal right before the first half would get the Green Wave within a score, as they trailed 17-10.

Harris picked up his second one-yard rushing touchdown to open up the third, building the Wildcat lead to 24-10.

Tulane would grab another big field goal, this time from 53-yards out, to make things 24-13.

In the fourth, Johnson would pick up another rushing touchdown, this one for 12 yards, to extend the 'Cats lead to 31-13.

A 25-yard touchdown reception with just under three minutes left in the game would see Tulane cut the lead down to 31-20, but they would be unable to come any closer as K-State secured the win.

Johnson was 21-for-28 with 227 yards in the air, 152 yards on the ground and two rushing touchdowns.

On the defense, Darien Whitaker picked up 1.5 sacks and 1.5 tackles for loss. Gabe Powers also had 1.5 tackles for loss.

The 'Cats will open up conference play next weekend when they travel out to Cincinnati to take on the Bearcats. Kickoff is set for 6 p.m.

articles.title: Neal Shipley holds onto 1-shot lead over Ben Kohles the Biltmore Championship Asheville
articles.summary: Neal Shipley held onto a one-shot lead over Ben Kohles on Saturday in the inaugural Biltmore Championship Asheville, making an eagle and a birdie on the two...
articles.body:
ASHEVILLE, N.C. — Neal Shipley held onto a one-shot lead over Ben Kohles on Saturday in the inaugural Biltmore Championship Asheville, making an eagle and a birdie on the two back-nine par 5s in his third straight bogey-free round.

Shipley had a 21-under 192 total on The Cliffs at Walnut Grove.

"Just going to keep doing what I'm doing," Shipley said. "Keep being me and keep having fun out there. Keep that mindset of going out there, chasing birdies, and trying to get it as low as possible tomorrow."

The PGA Tour rookie also opened with a 65 and had a 62 on Friday in the first of eight tournaments in the FedEx Cup Fall that determine the top 100 in the FedEx Cup who keep full cards for next season.

Shipley entered the week 183rd in the standings. A victory would not only give him a two-year exemption, it would secure him for the more lucrative Championship Series in 2028 when the tour revamps its schedule.

"It would be huge," Shipley said. "It would take a lot of stress off my back, that's for sure. It's one of those things I'm playing really well and I know it's a matter of time for me, so I'm going to give it my best shot tomorrow and lay it all out there and see what happens."

Kohles matched Shipley with a 65, birdieing three of the last four holes. Playing alongside Shipley in the final threesome, Kohles eagled the par-5 third. He's chasing his first PGA Tour title.

"Happy with the day," Kohles said. "Played solid. Took advantage of par 5s, which like I said yesterday, is something you got to do out here on this course."

Shipley hit a 227-yard approach to 7 1/2 to set up the eagle on the par-5 15th. He birdied the par-5 18th and closed with a par.

Eric Cole (64) and Ricky Castillo (65) were tied for third at 17 under. Jacob Bridgeman (64) and Max Greyserman (66) were 16 under.

The tee times were moved up and the players were grouped in threes because of the possibility of late afternoon storms.

The 21-year-old PGA Tour rookie rose up 13 spots on the leaderboard in Asheville thanks to a bogey-free 63 third round.

articles.title: New £1m grant to help protect Gloucestershire green spaces
articles.summary: The cash can be used by local communities to protect threatened green spaces and wildlife sites.
articles.body:
A £1m fund has been set up to help local communities protect threatened green spaces.

The Summerfield Charitable Trust said the money would help groups buy and safeguard local woodlands and wildlife sites when they come up for sale.

It is part of a new initiative from the Gloucestershire Nature and Climate Fund and the Gloucestershire Local Nature Partnership.

"We need an initiative like this now more than ever," said Diane Hill, chair of the Gloucestershire Nature and Climate Fund. "Once an important green space is lost, it can be lost for good."

Under pressure council 'seeking second bailout'

Fans line street for EMF star's final farewell

Hill said: "We know there are people across Gloucestershire who desperately want to protect woodland or wildlife sites in their community but when that land comes up for sale, they simply don't have the time or resources to compete with a private buyer.

"This funding means we can help them when it really matters.

"We can provide money to act quickly, bring in the legal and ecological expertise they need."

Recent examples of communities taking action to protect land include Daisybank , Lott Meadow and Southcourt Green, in Cheltenham, as well as Juniper Hill Field and Heavens Valley in Stroud .

Another was Rodborough Fields, near Stroud, where a public campaign to protect the woodland from development led to it being brought into community ownership.

John Bloxsom, chair of the Rodborough Fields and Frome Banks Preservation Group, said: "It's good news that a fund like this has been set up."

The group successfully bought nine acres of Rodborough Fields thanks to a Crowdfunding campaign that raised £200,000 but now the future of a further 30 acres is uncertain after it was put on the market this summer.

Bloxsom said that their latest bid had been rejected in favour of a rival bid from an unknown party, which was "causing concern in the community".

Angela France, one of the directors at Daisybank CIC, which helped to saved the field in Cheltenham from development last year, said she was "delighted" to hear about the new fund.

"Local green spaces are so important to us now," she said.

"I see more and more local communities getting together to protect them."

She said since buying the land, the group had organised litter picking, butterfly counts and an ecological survey in order to plan how best to maintain the field so that local wildlife could thrive.

A community event is also organised for 24 October to gather views on the future of the field.

The new fund has also been designed to contribute to nature recovery across the county, while addressing unequal access to nature.

David Owen, chair of trustees at The Summerfield Charitable Trust, said the initiative "has the potential to create a lasting legacy for nature, communities and future generations across Gloucestershire".

He added: "Through this investment, we hope to enable communities to act quickly when opportunities arise, protect important natural assets and create benefits for wildlife, health and wellbeing that will endure for many years to come."

articles.title: Online map shows how suitable Guernsey homes are for solar panels
articles.summary: The States of Guernsey says the map will show people how suitable for solar panels their homes are.
articles.body:
An online map has been launched to help islanders understand how suitable their homes are for solar panels.

The States of Guernsey said the map was colour-coded to show the amount of light that solar panels would receive on the island's rooftops across the course of a year.

Roofs with higher potential to generate electricity through solar panels show as dark red, while roof spaces with lower potential are coloured dark blue.

Deputy Adrian Gabriel, said while islanders are encouraged to contact professionals when looking to install solar panels, the map would be a "really helpful tool to get an initial idea on whether the potential for solar is there for householders".

The States said renewable energy provider, Little Green, had spoken to the Committee for the Environment & Infrastructure to highlight the benefits of the tool to people interested in installing solar panels.

Gabriel said the island gets about 30-35% more sunshine than the UK on average. He added: "This free tool makes us well placed to understand how we can better take advantage of the energy we can harness from the sun.

"It's clear that there is a significant opportunity in our island, and this map might just be the catalyst to take Guernsey's solar generation to the next level."

Simon de la Rue, commercial director at Little Green, said: "This map gives an independent, objective check, so any quote can be held to it."

articles.title: BMW PGA Championship prize money: What will the 2026 winner take home from Wentworth Club?
articles.summary: Rory McIlroy was among the contenders at the start of Sunday’s fourth round at Wentworth
articles.body:
The BMW PGA Championship comes to a conclusion at Wentworth Club on Sunday, with a stacked field chasing bumper prize money at the DP World Tour's flagship event.

The total tournament purse is $9m (£6.6m), with the winner in line to earn more than £1.1m.

As well as a healthy cheque, the tournament winner will also pick up a chunky 1,335 points to add to their tally in the DP World Tour's Order of Merit.

Rory McIlroy will be particularly motivated to scoop some points after losing ground to race leader and old foe Patrick Reed at the Irish Open.

Reed pulled out of the BMW PGA Championship with a hand injury, and McIlroy is in the mix on Sunday, beginning two shots back from the leaders in his bid to win a second title after his 2014 triumph at Wentworth.
